args.name: Assess an unfamiliar food sample
args.function: Provide a practical, evidence-producing method for investigating an unfamiliar food sample before deciding whether to eat it, distinguishing what the test establishes from what remains unknown.
args.conditions: Hazelnuts are visibly mature nearby, but I have no verified nutrition or toxicity findings for them. Known-safe roots remain available in my inventory. Avoid ingestion or exposure that could poison me; do not assume appearance establishes safety.
args.inputs: A gathered hazelnut sample if collection succeeds. Other required materials and prerequisites are unknown.
args.costs: Unknown; specify feasible material, effort and study costs, and any limits on what can be learned safely.
args.effects: An actual performed assessment should provide only findings supported by its method and conditions. If toxicity cannot be established safely with available means, state that limitation rather than declaring the food safe.

candidates.function: Crack the hard casing of your own shelled material, such as hazelnuts, in 0.1 blocks with controlled impacts of your own hard blunt striker on a stable support, and take the loose casing off opened blocks by hand to separate the kernel.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. target: your own unreserved, untreated item of a material with a represented casing (closed for crack modes, cracked unseparated for separate); quantity: exact tenths, 0.1-1 (default all, up to 1), reserved in one work (workId). Crack modes need striker (your own whole, rigid, sound inedible piece, e.g. a stone) and support (a solid inedible object in reach, not a plant or animal, or another own piece on firm ground), pinned for the work. Per 0.1 block: one cracking round, 1 energy; in crack-and-separate a block that opens adds one separation round, 0.5 energy; separate: one hand round, 0.5 energy per block. 0.9 units: at most 18 rounds, 13.5 energy. quoteOnly true reports quantity, striker condition, phases, maximum energy and wear bounds at no cost. pause, resume, cancel: one round, no energy. Checks run before any charge; failed rechecks pause open work at no charge. Travel and getting a striker are separate actions.
candidates.effects: Strength is hardness / 10; an impact passes the lower of striker and support strength x (1 - flexibility). At or below the casing strength the casing is unchanged: a real paid result that ends the work, the material returns as it was. Above it a block gains damage (load - strength) / strength: below 1 closed and damaged (a reattempt is new work), at 1 fractured open. Separation takes an opened block apart into 0.1 loose kernel and 0.1 casing fragments (a unit of each is that part of one whole unit) with the source origin, age and decay; the kernel carries all food value and toxicity, whatever they are. Opened blocks not separated stay cracked unseparated material. Wear: a striker no harder than what it strikes, or a support softer by 0.5 than what presses on it, loses 0.0001 kg per contact. Cancel returns reserved material as it now is; death leaves it at the worksite. Nothing is refunded, made safe or eaten; edibility, nutrition and toxins stay unknown; no reward.

candidates.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.

candidates.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
candidates.costs: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
candidates.effects: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

candidates.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
candidates.costs: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
candidates.effects: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

candidates.function: Scoop a little river or shallow water by hand and pour it onto the soil plot of a rooted plant whose measured soil is drier than it needs.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. collect (x, y: a visible ~ or = cell whose edge is within 0.65 m of you on the bank): 1 round, 0.3 energy; fills cupped hands to 0.2 L (or an owned water vessel given as container to its capacity). water (target: a rooted growing plant in reach; quantityLitres optional, default all held, at most 0.5): 1 round, 2 energy per litre poured (at least 0.05). status (target optional): 1 round, no energy. Refused before any cost, with the measured values, when soil moisture already meets the plant requirement (berry 0.6, root 0.5, tuber 0.8, fern-root 0.7), the plot is waterlogged (hazard waterlogging above 0.1 or moisture 1.3+), the target is not a rooted plant, or no water is held.
candidates.effects: Hand water is not an item: 40% of what is left leaks at each round end and 20% per metre walked; below 0.005 L it is gone. A pour loses 20% (from a vessel 5%) outside the root zone. The rest enters the root zone of the plant cell (1 m x 1 m, shared by every plant rooted there): 30 L raise soil moisture by 1; above 1.3 it runs off; above 1 half the excess drains each round; 10% evaporates each round (at most 0.0375 L). Soil moisture, which growth reads as min(1, moisture / requirement), includes it until it is gone. Growth is not boosted or promised. No reward.

candidates.function: Crush one of your own whole berries and rub its seeds free by hand, inspect a planting site, and sow the seeds in a small hand-loosened patch where they may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; pause, resume or cancel sowing.
candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.2 energy each. extract: target your own whole untreated berry item; one unit per attempt (quantity 1): 1 round, 0.5 energy. inspect: x, y a site in reach and/or target your own item or a sowing patch in reach: 1 round, 0.2 energy. sow: target your seed lot; x, y a site in reach on open ordinary soil (.), moisture 0.3-1.2, waterlogging at most 0.1, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 berry plants or patches being sown within 5 m. 2 rounds of 1 energy: loosen the patch, then place and cover the seeds; a loosened patch left by cancelled work needs only the second. pause, resume (workId), cancel: no energy. Refusals and failed rechecks cost nothing. No tool, vessel, water or soil is supplied.
candidates.effects: A whole berry unit (0.2 kg, food 8) is crushed: 0.01 kg of seeds (5 %, no food, no ageing) and 0.19 kg of pulp with all its food and age; both keep origin, harvest round and decay. The seeds of one unit are the one propagule the plant rules give one fruit unit; viability is unknown until something emerges. A unit whose parent is not a living berry plant has no represented seed: a paid failure, all pulp. Sowing moves the seeds from your inventory into the patch record, covered 5 mm deep in soil loosened 0.03 m. The patch gains establishment only from actual temperature (none at 6 C or below, full from 20 C), light, soil moisture (full from 0.6) and season; cold, darkness, drought or waterlogging stall it. At 12 a rooted seedling appears with no fruit (stock at most 4, the parent plant interval); fruit grows only under the existing growth rule; anyone may gather it. Watering a rooted plant is rooted-plant-watering. An unworked round pauses; cancel returns unsown seeds once and leaves loosened soil; death leaves them where you died. No reward or refund.
